None confirmed dead or access-blocked; these are evidence/remarkability leads, not blocked entries. Register candidates near the city centre are almost entirely the same ornamental cultivars already leaded above (reverse-geocoded this pass to Kassisaba/Tõnismäe residential streets and apartment courtyards, not parks; no age or story found for any, consistent with the existing pattern) or the far Kopli/Professorite küla oak cluster (5 plain 'Harilik tamm' entries around 59.458-59.462,24.664-24.669, unresearched, worth a future pass). DEEPEN pass 2026-09-12: the three 2017 Postimees/Olev Abner single-source leads below were followed up. Two now DELIVERED to data/research/tallinn-verified.json: tln_007 (A. Weizenbergi 26 guardhouse oak, still single-sourced for the specific age claim but corroborated in general terms by Kadriorg Park's own site) and tln_008 (Kopli kalmistupark oak, now genuinely two-sourced: Postimees plus tallinn.ee's own park page independently giving ~350 years and 'predates the cemetery'). blocked.reason: Sacred oak (hiis tradition), Metsakasti village, Viimsi parish, ~10km from Tallinn centre. Well documented: et.wikipedia.org gives 300 years old, 4.4m girth, 14m height, 8.8m root-collar girth, coordinates 59.49611,24.895; maavald.ee (Maavalla Koda's sacred-sites register) independently confirms it as a sacred site at the same village. BLOCKED on access, not on evidence: it stands on private farmland (Riiasoodi talu), and the site's own geocache page quotes the farm owner asking visitors not to enter the property, saying it can only be viewed from the roadside at a distance. BRIEF_RESEARCH.md's hard limit is private land not genuinely open to visitors, leave it out, and this is a verification pass rather than a judgement call about a view-only exception, so it is recorded here rather than delivered. A later pass could reassess it as a view-only entry with the pin set to the public roadside rather than the trunk.

Estonia's former thickest black poplar (698cm girth), stood in the Kaasani (Our Lady of Kazan) church yard at Liivalaia 38, coordinates 59.43028,24.75962 (et.wikipedia.org 'Kaasani kiriku pappel', matches the Wikidata individual-protected-object entry the brief surfaced almost exactly). Confirmed by a Postimees archive headline that it broke in a storm on 16 November 2004. No source found this pass confirming regrowth, a surviving stub, or current living status; the hard rule against publishing a tree known or suspected dead applies, so this is blocked rather than delivered. Also entangled in search results with a separate, related pair (Kanada pappel ja must pappel, KLO4000065, corner of Narva mnt/Weizenbergi, one specimen felled 2010, the other's current status unclear) which is a DIFFERENT location and should not be confused with this one in a future pass.

DEEPEN pass 2026-09-12. Postimees/Olev Abner (2017) named this Tallinn's SECOND OLDEST tree, ~370 years, behind the Presidential Palace/residence, A. Weizenbergi 39, Kadriorg. This pass found an individually-tagged OSM natural=tree node (id 4943448261) at 59.4380163,24.7937030, only about 15m from the Presidendi residents (Presidential residence) building centroid (59.4380108,24.7939143 per Overpass), carrying the note 'A solitary oak-tree, the eldest of an oak grove that stood here once for nearly four centuries' and a link to the old presidency website (vp2001-2006.president.ee, now dead/unresolvable). That note independently corroborates the tree's identity and age band even though the linked page could not be fetched. BLOCKED ON ACCESS rather than delivered: the presidential residence's own garden is walled off from the rest of Kadriorg park. A Postimees piece on the president's residential security (postimees.ee/3868615) and kadriorupark.ee's own page on the Chancellery building both describe the garden between Kadrioru Castle and the Presidential Chancellery as closed off with side walls, used for official representation, with only invited guests using the main entrance; this is a working government residence with a closed garden, not part of the free public park, so this fails the hard rule on private/access-restricted land. A later pass could reassess as a view-only entry only if a source specifically confirms the tree is visible from public ground outside the wall; nothing found this pass says so.

New find, DEEPEN pass 2026-09-12, surfaced while chasing the Kopli kalmistupark oak (tln_008). The same 2017 Postimees/Olev Abner list separately names a THIRD 360-year oak, distinct from the cemetery-park one, standing on the grounds of the Balti Laevaremonditehas (Baltic Ship Repair Plant) at Kopli 103, an active industrial shipyard roughly 1.5km from the cemetery park. Described elsewhere as a protected nature object with a 20m protection buffer from the trunk. BLOCKED ON ACCESS: this is a working industrial site (AS BLRT Grupp), not open ground the public may walk onto, so it fails the hard rule on private/access-restricted land regardless of the tree's own merit. Do not confuse with tln_008, the cemetery-park oak of the same age from the same article.
